craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta of closing dwelling; vyabhicāri peace at emblem-injunction (whole-WORK close). Sanskrit-first: ālambya (RESTING-ON — kept; support, not seat); dhyeya (TO-BE-CONTEMPLATED — kept; the work ends in the act it enjoins); śakti-catuṣka + triśūla-padma (FOUR POWERS + trident-lotus — emblem kept whole, unglossed). Rows: 10 (trident/lotus left standing), 9 (will/art/knowledge/power + trident/lotus six-rests catalogue), 1 (‘contemplated’ closes), 12 (whole-work śānta-fall). Close: ‘is to be contemplated’. Rupture: em-dash (resting turns to enjoining). Rejected: ‘meditated upon’ — killed: contemplated kept (house word); ‘seated upon’ — killed: resting kept; ‘fix the mind on’ — killed: contemplation kept nominal. Read aloud: THUS, REST-ing ON-will, ART, KNOW-ledge, POW-er, TRI-dent, LO-tus — BHAI-ra-va, the OWN-na-ture OF-all-THINGS, IS to BE-con-TEM-plat-ed.

lines: Thus, resting on will, art, knowledge, power, trident, lotus —
Bhairava, the own-nature of all things, is to be contemplated.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ittham icchākalājñānaśaktiśūlāmbujāśritaḥ | bhairavaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ pariśīlyate

reads_against.argmap: Upon what is Bhairava to be dwelt? → Emblem then injunction: trident-lotus Bhairava, all-nature, to be dwelt upon.
c1_essence: Trident-lotus emblem bearing four powers; Bhairava all-nature, to be dwelt upon.
